title: Introduce a sentinel layer variant for zstd:chunked pulls
body:
Introduce a sentinel layer variant to safely skip the full-digest mitigation for zstd:chunked pulls.

This PR eliminates the duality by creating a separate manifest variant with a non-tar sentinel layer prepended.  Unaware clients and scanners cannot process the sentinel variant so the image no longer has two possible interpretations.

Aware clients recognize the sentinel, skip it, and pull without the expensive full-digest recomputation safely because no unaware tool can be tricked into validating the wrong content.  Data layers are reused by digest so there is no duplication.

I've pushed an image with the new format here:  quay.io/giuseppe/zstd-chunked:sentinel

@mtrmac @actionmancan this is a PoC for the idea we have discussed on how to relax the mitigation

comments.body:
FWIW, just to have it written down, I think this is a few ~separate problem spaces, probably separate PRs.
- Add a _single-image-instance_ compression/decompression implementation for the new format. It needs a name, it needs to correctly compress, decompress, re-compress from/to gzip, _perhaps_ special-case conversions from/to current zstd:chunked . Ideally this should mostly fit into `copy/compression.go` (I don’t know how we add/remove the sentinel itself)
  - The manifest updates should go through `ManifestUpdateOptions`, or maybe we should finally give up on that one (and how it uses `BlobInfo` for edits) and move to an internal-only API. The latter, if it should happen, would certainly be a separate PR.
- Add the ability to enforce chunked-only pull path for an image (disable fallbacks, or fall back to a full pull to a temporary file + serving ranges from that). That would be ~inactive at that point, but conceptually a separate chunk of effort.
- Set up pulls of sentinel images to use the optimized path
- Figure out how we are going to build the "zstd as tar"+"zstd sentinel" images that share blobs.
  - … and a variant of #201 .

<s>@giuseppe looking at unrelated work… the sentinel resolves the duality of consuming the zstd:chunked native metadata (`storage/pkg/chunked/minimal.TOC` and the file entries) and zstd:chunked-visible file contents, vs. raw-tar metadata and file contents.

But… we added a third set of metadata, the tar-split. And on chunked pull, we create all files from native TOC metadata on disk, but on push, we use the tar-split.

So I think a user could pull a sentinel image, inspect the contents, see nothing unexpected, then re-push (for some reason; both pushing as gzip and as zstd:chunked), and the re-pushed images could have different metadata (e.g. something made set-UID).

Am I missing something?

If not, we’d also need some kind of consistency check between the tar-split data and the TOC (ugh)… or maybe make the tar-split data optional again to avoid the consistency check cost.
- That’s mildly annoying, because tar-split is currently ~mandatory. It would effectively be a major version of zstd:chunked again.
- I’m not sure we can do that at all, the on-disk storage can be lossy, e.g. with force_mask.</s>

> So I think a user could pull a sentinel image, inspect the contents, see nothing unexpected, then re-push (for some reason; both pushing as gzip and as zstd:chunked), and the re-pushed images could have different metadata (e.g. something made set-UID).
> 
> Am I missing something?
> 
> If not, we’d also need some kind of consistency check between the tar-split data and the TOC (ugh)… or maybe make the tar-split data optional again to avoid the consistency check cost.
> 
> * That’s mildly annoying, because tar-split is currently ~mandatory. It would effectively be a major version of zstd:chunked again.

my hope/plan for the longer term is to drop the tarSplit data completely from the zstd:chunked, as it is really ugly to have 3 ways to store the same metadata.  One way to achieve it is to use a canonical tarball representation and enforce it for zstd:chunked (I've played with it here: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/compare/main...giuseppe:container-libs:canonical-tarball some time ago).

I've also lost some context after so long time and I need to look again at all the details, but isn't the validation we already have for the tarSplit enough to catch mismatches with the TOC (`ensureTOCMatchesTarSplit`) or what other kind of attack is possible?

We calculate the zstd:chunked TOC based on the tar stream, a local podman client can't be tricked to push a TOC with different metadata that is in the tarsplit.  If the tarsplit is malicious we wouldn't get the same UncompressedDigest once the tarball is created.

> * I’m not sure we can do that at all, the on-disk storage can be lossy, e.g. with force_mask.

when `force_mask` is used, we must mount the layer before accessing it so that the right metadata is applied, but I hope we don't need to get there

> I've also lost some context after so long time and I need to look again at all the details, but isn't the validation we already have for the tarSplit enough to catch mismatches with the TOC (`ensureTOCMatchesTarSplit`)

Oh, right! I have completely forgotten this already exists. So we are fine. Thanks!
